newsitem.title: UK: National Power appoints Collins chairman.
newsitem.headline: National Power appoints Collins chairman.

text.p: National Power, Britain's biggest electricity generator, said on Tuesday that chairman John Baker was retiring next year, and it was appointing Sir John Collins as his successor.
Baker, chairman since April 1995, played a major role in the privatisation of Britain's electricity industry and the creation of National Power in 1990.
He will retire in December at the age of 60.
Collins, 55, joined the National Power board as a non-executive director on October 1, 1996.

A former chairman and chief executive of oil giant Shell UK, he is also currently a director of British satellite broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc and NM Rothschild & Sons, and chairman of drugs group Cantab Pharmaceuticals Plc.

"The board believes that Sir John and chief executive Keith Henry will together provide a winning combination to lead National Power successfully into the next phase of its development," Baker said in a statement.
"In the meantime, we will be working closely together to ensure the company maintains its drive to compete strongly in the UK and to build on our increasingly successful overseas business," he added.
